title: When Faith Looked Like Disobedience
paragraphs:
When Faith Looked Like Disobedience
Joshua 6:3–5

Jericho did not fall with a sword first.
It fell with a strange command.

March?
Silently?
For days?
To the watching eye, this looked ridiculous. Almost rebellious. Almost weak. Almost like Joshua had misunderstood God completely.

Because when a city stands in front of you, human instinct says attack.
God said walk.
And that is the scandal of faith: sometimes obedience to God looks like disobedience to human logic.

Imagine the soldiers. Trained for combat, not processions. Built for battle cries, not quiet circles around impossible walls. Every lap around Jericho may have felt foolish. Every silent step may have looked like delay. But heaven was not stalling. Heaven was setting the stage.

Because God was doing more than bringing down walls.
He was bringing down self-reliance.

Israel would not be able to say, “We won because we were stronger.”
No.
When the walls fell, only one name could be praised:
The Lord.
And that still happens now.

Sometimes God tells you to forgive when revenge feels stronger.
To wait when urgency is screaming.
To stay when your pride wants to leave.
To give when fear says hoard.
To pray when your flesh wants to panic.

It feels backward.
It feels costly.
It can even look, to other people, like you are doing it wrong.
But here’s what we miss: faith is not proven when God’s command makes sense. Faith is proven when it doesn’t, and you obey anyway.
Joshua 6 reminds us that God does not need our cleverness to fulfill His promise. He wants our surrender. He wants trust that keeps walking, even before the wall shows one crack.
And that points us to Jesus.

Because the cross also looked wrong.
Like defeat.
Like weakness.
Like heaven’s silence.
But what looked like loss was actually victory. What looked like shame became salvation. And through Christ, God turned the greatest apparent failure in history into the triumph that saves sinners.

So if obedience feels strange right now, do not mistake unusual for unfaithful.
If God has spoken in His Word, keep walking.
Keep trusting.
Keep circling what has not fallen yet.
The wall will not stand forever before the God who keeps His promises.

Faith sometimes looks foolish before it looks fruitful.
But obedience never returns empty in the hands of God.

Jesus is still the One who leads His people through impossible places.
Jesus is still the One who tears down what we cannot move.
Jesus is still the hope for those tired of marching around unanswered prayers.

So do not quit on lap six.
Grace may be waiting on lap seven.

Prayer:
Lord, when Your commands confront my logic, teach me to obey anyway. Break my pride, crush my self-reliance, and make me trust You more than appearances. And when my heart trembles before walls too strong for me, fix my eyes on Christ—the One who won victory through what looked like defeat. In Jesus’ name, amen.
